thread:
alex: Heads-up: after enabling FP8 path + AWQ weights for gpt-j-6B on the dedicated pool, we saw sporadic OOMs during long-context generation (~4k tokens). Only reproducible under mixed batch sizes (2-10).

maria: interesting. Is the KV cache stored as fp16 or fp32 for that run? FP8 + fp16 cache could trigger lots of casts.

alex: kv cache was fp16 by default on that pool. Stack from the runtime logs:  
```
[mem] gpu_total=40G gpu_free_at_start=34.2G
[alloc] arena_reserved=18.0G arena_peak=17.6G free_frag=3.8G
[kv_cache(dtype=float16)]=11.3G
[weights_awq]=6.2G
[temp_deq_fp32]=2.1G
[workspace_needed(tiling)]=1.8G
OOM at allocation size=512MB
```

sophia: likely causes: (a) allocator fragmentation (arena not returning big slabs), (b) FP8/AWQ kernels dequantizing into fp32 intermediates, and (c) tiled GEMM path picking a workspace-hungry kernel for some batch shapes.

tom: quick test: switch allocator to "cuda_malloc" (no arena) and force qkernel variant that accumulates in int32. Peak drops but latency jitter increases. We got ~900MB lower peak.

maria: can you share the exact env flags you toggled? we should be able to flip in prod pools for mitigation.

tom: sure:
```
REDWOOD_ALLOCATOR=malloc
REDWOOD_WS_MAX_BYTES=1610612736  # 1.5GB per-request workspace cap
REDWOOD_QKERNEL_HINT=q8_acc_int32
REDWOOD_KV_DTYPE=fp16
REDWOOD_BUFFER_REUSE=1
```

alex: malloc allocator reduced fragmentation but made small allocations slower. Not ideal long-term. Also noticed increased PCIe traffic when host-spill occurred.

sophia: for a durable fix we should: 1) build per-model memory profiles (weights, kv dtype, worst-case kernel workspace); 2) teach the scheduler to pick kernel variants based on pool remaining slab size and per-request workspace budget; 3) implement a spill-to-host path for temporary dequantization buffers that are > X MB.

maria: adding: add a per-request transient cap and an early-reject with a clear console warning: "request requires Y GB workspace, only Z GB allocable". Less surprising for customers.

ci-bot: deploy: canary updated (awq-fp8-allocator-hotfix) — 4 hosts reporting healthy, 1 host in degraded state :warning:

tom: profiling command I used to capture allocator traces and kernel selection timeline:
```
RT_PROFILE=mem:timeline,allocs RT_DEBUG_KERNS=1 REDWOOD_DEBUG_ALLOC=1 ./bin/runtime --model gpt-j-6B-awq --batch 6 --seq 4096
```

sophia: from those traces I implemented a heuristic prototype: if tiled-gemm workspace > 25% of free_arena, route to streaming-gemm with slightly higher compute cost but much lower workspace. That avoided OOMs in our synthetic repro. Will PR today.

alex: excellent. I'll open a perf test that hits the long-context AWQ path and validates: peak memory < 90% allocable and P99 latency within 1.2x baseline. Also add a test case where kv_cache forced to fp32 to compare counters.

maria: note for ops: you can temporarily set REDWOOD_KV_FORCE_FP32=true on the pool to avoid repeated incidents while we land kernel routing. It increases steady-state footprint but reduces dequant transient peaks.

sophia: long-term kernel work: audit all q8/awq kernels for temp allocation patterns: avoid materializing full fp32 deq buffers where possible. Consider fused attention that dequantizes just the tiles in-flight. Also evaluate FP8 inference path to ensure accumulator dtype choices don't blow memory.

tom: action items:
- sophia: PR for kernel routing heuristic (in review)
- alex: perf test + repro job (blocked until CI slot)
- maria: ops toggle + dashboard alert when workspace_needed > 70% of allocable
- infra: investigate a slab-return optimization for the arena allocator to reduce fragmentation

alex: thanks all. keeping this open until kernel routing and perf test land. Ping here for any regressions after enabling the heuristic. :rocket:
